# Introduction

The [World Cup hosting premium analysis](../world-cup-hosting-premium/index.qmd) controls for each team's strength going into a tournament via `pre_elo_rating`. That covariate isn't part of the Kaggle matches dataset, so it's sourced separately here, in its own post, for the same reason the match-cleaning steps live in their own post: it keeps the scrape traceable and reproducible independent of any downstream analysis.

::: {.callout-note}
## Data attribution
All Elo ratings on this page are sourced from [**eloratings.net**](https://eloratings.net), the World Football Elo Ratings project. All credit for the underlying rating methodology and data collection belongs to that site — this post only documents how the publicly served data is downloaded and reshaped for analysis here.
:::

# Data source

[eloratings.net](https://eloratings.net) publishes a "starting" Elo snapshot for every year, e.g. [https://eloratings.net/2026_start](https://eloratings.net/2026_start). The page itself renders client-side (a JS grid) and has no public API, but the grid is populated from two plain TSV files that can be read directly:

- `https://eloratings.net/{year}_start.tsv` — one row per team, ranked by rating, with 31 tab-separated columns: rank-change arrow, rank, team code, rating, highest/average/lowest rank and rating, rank/rating changes over the trailing 3 months, 6 months, 1, 2, 5, and 10 years, total matches played (home/away/neutral), wins/losses/draws, and goals for/against.
- `https://eloratings.net/en.teams.tsv` — maps each 2-letter team code to its full country name.

```{python}
from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd
```

```{python}
_HEADERS = {"User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0"}
_BASE_URL = "https://eloratings.net"

_RATINGS_COLUMNS = [
    "rank_chg", "rank", "team_code", "rating",
    "rank_max", "rating_max", "rank_avg", "rating_avg", "rank_min", "rating_min",
    "rank_3m_change", "rating_3m_change",
    "rank_6m_change", "rating_6m_change",
    "rank_1y_change", "rating_1y_change",
    "rank_2y_change", "rating_2y_change",
    "rank_5y_change", "rating_5y_change",
    "rank_10y_change", "rating_10y_change",
    "matches_total", "matches_home", "matches_away", "matches_neutral",
    "wins", "losses", "draws", "goals_for", "goals_against",
]

def get_starting_elo_ratings(year: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Download each country's starting Elo rating (and full rating history) for a given World Cup year."""
    ratings = pd.read_csv(
        f"{_BASE_URL}/{year}_start.tsv",
        sep="\t", header=None,
        names=_RATINGS_COLUMNS,
        keep_default_na=False,
        storage_options=_HEADERS,
    )
    teams = pd.read_csv(
        f"{_BASE_URL}/en.teams.tsv",
        sep="\t", header=None, usecols=[0, 1],
        names=["team_code", "country"],
        keep_default_na=False,
        storage_options=_HEADERS,
    )
    ratings = ratings.merge(teams, on="team_code", how="left")
    ratings["year"] = year
    other_columns = [c for c in _RATINGS_COLUMNS if c not in ("team_code", "rating")]
    return ratings[["year", "country", "team_code", "rating", *other_columns]]
```

# Building the panel

Starting Elo ratings are pulled for every calendar year from 1930 through 2026 — not just World Cup years — and stacked into a single panel, so downstream posts can look up any team's rating in any year without re-scraping. Years already present in the output file from a previous run are skipped, so re-running this post only hits eloratings.net for new years.

```{python}
_DATA_PATH = Path('./data/elo_ratings.parquet')
years = range(1930, 2027)

if _DATA_PATH.exists():
    cached_ratings = pd.read_parquet(_DATA_PATH)
    cached_years = set(cached_ratings['year'])
else:
    cached_ratings = pd.DataFrame()
    cached_years = set()

missing_years = [year for year in years if year not in cached_years]

if missing_years:
    new_ratings = pd.concat(
        [get_starting_elo_ratings(year) for year in missing_years],
        ignore_index=True,
    )
    elo_ratings = pd.concat([cached_ratings, new_ratings], ignore_index=True)
else:
    elo_ratings = cached_ratings
```

# Normalizing country names

```{python}
normalized_country_names = {'United States':'United States of America', 
                            'West Germany':'Germany FR',
                            'East Germany':'Germany DR',
                            'Ireland':'Republic of Ireland',
                            'Iran':'IR Iran',
                            'China':'China PR',
                            'South Korea':'Republic of Korea',
                            'North Korea':"Democratic People's Republic of Korea",
                            'Czechia':'Czech Republic'}

elo_ratings['country'] = elo_ratings['country'].replace(normalized_country_names)

# Replace the appearence of Russia before its creation
mask = (elo_ratings['year'] <= 1991) & (elo_ratings['country'].str.contains('Russia'))
elo_ratings.loc[mask, ['country', 'team_code']] = ['Soviet Union', 'SU']

```

# Output

The combined panel — sourced from [eloratings.net](https://eloratings.net) — is written out for downstream use by the data-cleaning and hosting-premium posts:

```{python}
elo_ratings.to_parquet(_DATA_PATH)
```

# Visual check

As a sanity check that the scrape actually worked, here's Elo rating over time for two teams read straight back from the parquet file:

```{python}
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

saved_ratings = pd.read_parquet(_DATA_PATH)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4.5))

for team, color in [("Argentina", "#2a78d6"), ("France", "#eb6834")]:
    team_ratings = saved_ratings[saved_ratings["country"] == team].sort_values("year")
    ax.plot(team_ratings["year"], team_ratings["rating"], label=team, color=color, linewidth=2)

ax.set_xlabel("Year")
ax.set_ylabel("Starting Elo rating")
ax.set_title("Starting Elo rating by year")
ax.legend(frameon=False)
ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)

fig.tight_layout()
```
